author: massicomar
title: Independent Set
summary:
There is a tree with $N$ vertices, numbered $1, 2, \ldots, N$. For each $i$ ($1 \leq i \leq N - 1$), the $i$-th edge connects Vertex $x_i$ and $y_i$.

Taro has decided to paint each vertex in white or black. Here, it is not allowed to paint two adjacent vertices both in black.

Find the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo $10^9 + 7$.

Input

Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:

$N$
$x_1$ $y_1$
$x_2$ $y_2$
$:$
$x_{N - 1}$ $y_{N - 1}$

Output

Print the number of ways in which the vertices can be painted, modulo $10^9 + 7$.
explanation: Root the tree; for each vertex keep the count of colourings of its subtree for each of its two colours.
traps: Recursion depth 1e5 can overflow the stack on a path-shaped tree.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[v][c] = number of valid colourings of v's subtree with v coloured c (white/black)
dp[v] = number of valid colourings of v's subtree
options.why: The parent needs to know whether v is black.

options.text: dp[mask] = whether the black set mask is independent
dp[d] = number of colourings of the vertices at depth d
options.why: Edges connect parent/child, so depth layers aren't independent.

extraLayers.explanation: The only interaction across an edge is 'not both black', so the parent needs v's colour.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[v][white] = Π (dp[u][white] + dp[u][black]); dp[v][black] = Π dp[u][white] over children u

options.why: Children's subtrees are independent: multiply, don't add.
A black v forbids black children.

extraLayers.explanation: Independent subtrees multiply; a black vertex forces white children.

es.explanation: Enraíza el árbol; para cada vértice guarda la cantidad de coloreos de su subárbol para cada uno de sus dos colores.
traps: Una recursión de profundidad 1e5 puede desbordar la pila si el árbol es un camino.

dp-state.explanation: Lo único que pasa de un lado a otro de una arista es “no las dos negras”, así que el padre necesita el color de v.

why.b: El padre necesita saber si v es negro.
why.d: Las aristas unen padre e hijo, así que los niveles de profundidad no son independientes.

dp-transition.explanation: Los subárboles independientes se multiplican; un vértice negro obliga a que sus hijos sean blancos.

why.b: Los subárboles de los hijos son independientes: se multiplica, no se suma.
why.c: Si v es negro, sus hijos no pueden ser negros.
